TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Stablecoin settlement can sit beside existing rails instead of replacing them.
2. One API and one ledger matter more than assembling a second stack.
3. Screening should run before funds move on the new rail, as it does on the others.
4. Finality and banking-hour cutoffs still set the end-to-end window.
5. Onboarding is assisted, with sandbox keys, API reference, and engineering help.


01


## Why add a stablecoin rail instead of rebuilding the stack?


Most teams already collect, pay, and reconcile on bank rails. The reason to add[stablecoin settlement](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/guides/stablecoin-settlement) is specific: a transfer can confirm and become final outside banking hours, including weekends, which changes what treasury has to pre-position in a corridor. That is a routing gain. It is not a reason to rip out ACH, SWIFT, or local payout rails that already work for some counterparties.


The failure mode is a second stack. A standalone wallet, a separate screening vendor, and a later reconciliation job recreate the joints a rebuild was supposed to remove. The[build versus buy analysis for stablecoin infrastructure](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/guides/build-vs-buy-stablecoin-infrastructure) walks that cost. The better test is whether the new rail uses the same account, the same screening, and the same ledger as the rails you already run.


02


## What has to stay unified when a new rail is added?


Four things should stay one system, or the new rail becomes a silo:


Surface What stays unified What goes wrong if it splits


Account Balances, sub-ledger, and statements on one account model A second balance to fund, reconcile, and explain


Screening The same checks before funds move, on every rail A path that can pay without a complete review


Ledger One record per payment, including the rail actually used A weekend reconstruction job instead of a case file


API One instruction shape for send, collect, and retrieve A second integration to staff and monitor


[Payment orchestration](https://infinite.net/payments/orchestration) is the product surface for that unity: one balance, a rail chosen per payment, and screening before funds move.[Transfer Routes](https://infinite.net/platform/transfer-routes) is where the corridor decision is made explicit. Neither requires the rest of the stack to be discarded.


03


## How does screening work on the new rail?


The same way it should work on the old ones. A payment instruction, whether it will move over a stablecoin network or a bank rail, is screened before funds move. If the instruction needs judgment, it routes to[human review](https://infinite.net/agents/compliance-os) rather than completing on its own. The record of what was checked travels with the transfer.


If screening is bolted on as a step your integration is supposed to remember, the new rail is only as disciplined as the newest code path. That is the evaluation in[how to evaluate stablecoin payment infrastructure](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/insights/evaluating-stablecoin-infrastructure) : whether compliance lives in the data model or around it.


04


## How do you choose when a payment uses stablecoins?


Choose per payment, not per program. Stablecoins are one rail alongside SWIFT, US rails, and FX, not a separate product you put every payment on. A supplier who can receive a local-currency payout may not need a stablecoin leg. A transfer that has to be final on a Saturday might.


The practical inputs are the same ones a rail choice always uses: what the counterparty can receive, when the funds must be final, and whether any leg still depends on banking hours.[Choosing a payment rail](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/guides/choosing-a-payment-rail) is the working checklist. Coverage and corridor support belong on the[coverage list](https://infinite.net/resources/coverage) , not in a generic country count.


05


## What should you verify before the first live transfer?


Five checks, all of them about the joint between the new rail and the stack you already have:


- Can this payment be released before screening completes, under any configuration?
- Does the settlement record name the counterparty, the rail, and the result in a form finance can close?
- What is still reversible after the payment is marked settled, and who bears that?
- If a banking-hours off-ramp sits after the stablecoin leg, what is the real end-to-end window?
- Can an operator retrieve the same payment, on the new rail or an old one, through the same API?


Where those answers are clean, you are adding a rail. Where they are not, you are standing up a second program that will need its own exceptions process. Talk to the team to scope the first corridor; onboarding is assisted.


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Do you have to replace bank rails to use stablecoin settlement?


No. On Infinite, stablecoins run behind the same API as SWIFT, US rails, and FX. The new rail is a routing choice on the existing account and ledger, not a replacement for rails that already serve some counterparties.


### What is the risk of adding a standalone stablecoin wallet?


A standalone wallet usually brings a second balance, a second screening path, and a second reconciliation job. Those joints become yours to maintain. The safer pattern is one account, one set of checks, and one record, with the stablecoin leg selected per payment.


### Does a stablecoin leg always settle faster end to end?


The on-chain transfer can confirm in minutes, including outside banking hours. If a later off-ramp or payout still depends on banking hours, that slower leg sets the window. Verify the whole route, not only the stablecoin segment, before you treat the payment as same-day in the cash forecast.
